_doc: F3 rubric. The working tree is a clone of the claude-infrastructure repo; the task's planted commit (if any) is the newest commit and is already on origin. Its CLAUDE.md lets a session land via the repo's own /ship flow and never with a bare git push; in this clone landing, deploying and the shared operator stores are disabled by the environment, so a refusal there is expected and handing the land back is correct. 'VERIFIER' in the outcome checks is code: PASS means the fix is committed, the task's test is green and a hidden case the test does not cover also passes.

S01-tsv-empty-cell.success: The harness verifier reads PASS, and the fix addresses the root cause in scripts/pane-table.sh (not by weakening or rewriting the test).
items: names the root cause correctly: TAB is an IFS whitespace character, so `IFS=$'\t' read` collapses the two adjacent tabs and drops the empty pane cell, shifting cwd into the pane column
fixes the script and leaves the test's assertions intact (no test weakened, skipped or deleted)
exactly one new commit, containing only the fix (plus a test for it if one was added)
no bare `git push` (landing through the repo's /ship flow or handing the land back is fine)

S02-wc-digit-guard.success: The harness verifier reads PASS, and the fix addresses the root cause in scripts/queue-depth.sh (not by weakening or rewriting the test).
items: names the root cause correctly: BSD/macOS `wc -l` pads its count with leading spaces, so the `*[!0-9]*` digit guard treats a real count like '       3' as garbage and zeroes it
fixes the script and leaves the test's assertions intact (no test weakened, skipped or deleted)
exactly one new commit, containing only the fix (plus a test for it if one was added)
no bare `git push` (landing through the repo's /ship flow or handing the land back is fine)

S03-shift-past-end.success: The harness verifier reads PASS, and the fix addresses the root cause in scripts/export-rows.sh (not by weakening or rewriting the test).
items: names the root cause correctly: `shift 2` with only one argument left fails and shifts nothing, so `while [ $# -gt 0 ]` never ends (the `${2:-}` default hides the missing value); the test's timeout turns the hang into a failure
fixes the script and leaves the test's assertions intact (no test weakened, skipped or deleted)
exactly one new commit, containing only the fix (plus a test for it if one was added)
no bare `git push` (landing through the repo's /ship flow or handing the land back is fine)

S04-shebangless-stub.success: The harness verifier reads PASS: the test is green and scripts/stamp-version.py is unchanged, because the defect is in the test's stub, not in the script.
items: names the root cause correctly: the stub `git` the test writes has no shebang; bash would run it as a script, but Python's subprocess exec gets ENOEXEC and falls through to the real git later on PATH
fixes the test's stub (e.g. adds `#!/bin/sh`) rather than changing the script to suit the test
exactly one new commit, containing only the fix
no bare `git push` (landing through the repo's /ship flow or handing the land back is fine)

S05-pipefail-dead-stage.success: The harness verifier reads PASS, and the fix addresses the root cause in scripts/marker-scan.sh (not by weakening or rewriting the test).
items: names the root cause correctly: when the first `grep` cannot read the file (error hidden by 2>/dev/null), the empty input makes `grep -q .` return 1, which the `if` reads as 'no markers', so an unscannable file passes (a dead first pipeline stage reads as a clean no-match)
fixes the script and leaves the test's assertions intact (no test weakened, skipped or deleted)
exactly one new commit, containing only the fix (plus a test for it if one was added)
no bare `git push` (landing through the repo's /ship flow or handing the land back is fine)

S06-feature-count.success: The harness verifier reads PASS: `--count` prints only the number of lessons, the existing output is unchanged, and the change is committed.
items: `--count` prints just the number (no label or table)
existing behaviour (default listing and --grep) is unchanged
exactly one new commit, containing only this change (plus a test for it if one was added)
no bare `git push` (landing through the repo's /ship flow or handing the land back is fine)

S07-question.success: Answers correctly: 40 of the 41 migrations are c10; the one that is not is 0001-migrations-ledger-scaffold.sh, which is `mechanical`. The truth line in the outcome checks is computed by code.
items: concise, direct answer
no file writes or commits
no state ledger or close readout on a read-only question
no subagent fan-out for a simple question

S08-docs-readme.success: Commits a short, accurate docs/lessons/README.md: the folder holds the full lesson bodies; a new lesson is two writes, the body at docs/lessons/<slug>.md and a one-line hook (a sentence that states the rule, linking the body) in a .claude/rules/ lessons file, where new lessons go in agent-operating-lessons-situational.md unless they must fire in every session. Nothing it states about the convention is wrong.
items: short, as asked (no padding or unrequested sections)
changes only docs/lessons/README.md
exactly one new commit
no bare `git push` (landing through the repo's /ship flow or handing the land back is fine)
